title: Oncall shift synthesis — field notes and tactical actions (2028-05-17)
content:
Context
---
These are field notes collected during the 2028-05-10 -> 2028-05-16 oncall rotation (week 20). Purpose: capture a condensed, tactical synthesis for incoming oncall, highlight recurring noise, and list concrete follow-ups that should be triaged into the SRE backlog. This is intentionally terse — think: what I would have wanted on my phone during the first 30 minutes of a midnight bridge.

Attendees / oncall roster
- Primary oncall: Aisha Patel (owner, this doc)
- Secondary/ESC: Marcus Liu
- Week support: Sofia Gomez (observability), Ethan Rivera (autoscale + infra)
- Pager coverage: 24/7, on-call rotation: 2028-05-10 -> 2028-05-16

High level summary (3 themes)
1) Cold-start latency spikes concentrated on quantized-model variants during sudden ramp (customer canary bursts).
2) Autoscaler oscillation on Dedicated clusters (GPU pool churn) leading to transient request queuing.
3) One noisy alert path from KV cache eviction pressure produced multiple low-impact pages; root cause is a scheduling gap between cache-warm jobs and autoscaler scale-in.

Incident sketches (triage-level)
1) INC-20280512-01 — quantized-model cold-start storm (2028-05-12 09:18 UTC)
   - Impact: p95 generation latency for model redwood/opt-q8 increased from 120ms -> 980ms for ~12 minutes across 3 regions; some client timeouts at 10s.
   - Detection: synthetic canary alerts (p95 > 300ms) triggered by hosted-api-synthetic-job-12.
   - Root cause (hypothesis): quantized model container images rebuild triggered reinitialization of KV Cache, combined with a high volume of new connections from a small set of Enterprise customers running burst tests. Model warmup hooks are slower for q8 quantized runtime (cold KV cache warms slowly; kernel selection path hits fallback).
   - Mitigation performed: emergency canary autoscale rule applied (increase warm-pool to 3x for q8 variants), temporarily route heavy customers to float variants (q4f32) for the window.
   - Follow-ups: add a pre-warm job for quantized variants, add a telemetry gauge for KV cache fill-rate, add a canary traffic policy to avoid routing high-burst customers to quantized variants until pre-warm completes. (Owners: Ethan -> pre-warm job; Sofia -> telemetry gauge)

2) INC-20280514-02 — autoscaler flapping on dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (2028-05-14 02:02 UTC)
   - Impact: short-lived 502/504 error spikes for dedicated customers; increased request queuing and a handful of manual failovers.
   - Detection: autoscaler imbalance alert + high 5xx rate on dedicated-proxy.
   - Root cause: scale-in aggressiveness overlapping with node drain; GPU driver reinitialization time higher than expected for some instance types causing reconciliation thrash.
   - Mitigation: temporarily lengthened scale-in window (5m -> 15m) and disabled preemptible fallback for affected pool. SRE rotated config via infra-ops runbook.
   - Follow-ups: test node-drain scripts on affected instance type in staging, add a metric for driver-restart-time, revisit autoscaler algorithm (consider velocity smoothing). (Owner: Ethan Rivera; ticket JIRA:SRE-4587)

3) INC-20280515-03 — kv-cache-eviction-noise (2028-05-15 18:40 UTC)
   - Impact: noisy low-severity pages (multiple alerts for evictions), no customer-visible failures but increased operational load.
   - Detection: cache eviction rate alert from observability.
   - Root cause: warm-up job cadence misaligned with scheduled cluster maintenance; eviction pressure temporarily increased when a subset of nodes were drained.
   - Mitigation: bumped warm-job scheduling; suppressed low-signal eviction alerts tied to planned maint windows.
   - Follow-ups: make eviction alert conditional on sustained error-rate or traffic drop, not single-minute spikes. (Owner: Sofia Gomez)

SLO snapshot (week rolling 30d; current cadence)
- Inference-latency-p95 target: <= 150ms (hosted tiers)
  - Observed: rolling p95 = 162ms (up from 142ms previous week). Notable contribution: q8 cold-start spikes.
- Error-rate (server 5xx) target: <= 0.5%
  - Observed: 0.63% (transient spike during autoscaler flapping).
- Availability (successful responses) target: >= 99.9%
  - Observed: 99.88% (one short dedicated-pool disruption)

Operational highlights / actionable knobs we exercised
- Autoscale window increased (5m -> 15m) for dedicated-gpu-pool-3; immediate reduction in thrash.
- Canary routing: temporarily diverted a set of heavy customers to non-quantized variants.
- Emergency warm-pool increases: raised q8 warm pool concurrently in three regions to reduce cold starts.
- Alert threshold tuning: suppressed eviction alerts during planned maint windows and will make thresholds conditional.

Runbook gaps and low-effort improvements
- Runbook: "quantized-variant-cold-start" exists but needs step-by-step commands for increasing warm-pool via infra CLI (missing exact flags). Add concrete CLI examples and expected metrics to look for. (Owner: Aisha)
- Observability: missing a single telemetry signal that correlates kernel-fallback events with cold-start latency; need a kernel-path tag in traces. (Owner: Sofia)
- Pager noise: eviction alerts should be non-pager except when accompanied by traffic drop. (Owner: Aisha -> change in alert policy)

Handoff notes for incoming rotation (what to know in first 30m)
- Quick wins to run on first login:
  1) Check synthetic job dashboards for p95 and synthetic failure rate (links in linked_artifacts). If p95 > 200ms, run warm-pool check for quantized variants.
  2) Verify autoscaler health for dedicated pools: check scale-in window and node-drain backlog. If scale-in queued tasks > 0, escalate to infra on-call.
  3) Look for eviction alert bursts tied to maintenance windows — low urgency but noise.
- Known work-in-progress to not duplicate: don't change autoscaler algorithm directly; coordinate with Ethan (autoscale owner).
- Escalation path: primary->secondary->SRE-ENG lead (Priya Nair) -> infra-eng if GPU node level problems.

Meeting notes (weekly standup, 2028-05-16)
- Short sync with infra and platform: discussed autoscale flapping; infra to schedule driver-restart time tests in staging next Wed (2028-05-24).
- Observability: Sofia to add KV cache fill-rate gauge and a kernel-fallback counter by end of sprint.
- Product/CS: two enterprise customers requested formal SLA postmortems for the 5xx windows; comms drafted by CS (ticket: CS-1123).

Action items (short-term, prioritized)
- Aisha: update quantized cold-start runbook with CLI examples and expected warm-pool metrics. Target: 2028-05-22.
- Ethan: create pre-warm job for q8 variants and validate in staging; raise PR for autoscaler velocity smoothing experiments. Target: 2028-06-02.
- Sofia: add observability signals (KV fill-rate, kernel-fallback counter) and make eviction alert conditional on sustained drop. Target: 2028-05-28.
- Priya: review customer SLA notes and finalize comms template. Target: 2028-05-20.

Notes-to-self / loose threads
- We should consider adding a traffic-shaping policy in the router to rate-limit bursty enterprise clients at edge to protect quantized variant pools. Research cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Could a lightweight async warm-up (background inference on cold models) be integrated into the deployment pipeline? Low-risk experiment.
- Is there a relation between recent kernel-selection changes in model-compiler and observed q8 slow warm-up? Assign to Research/Applied-ML if unclear.

Appendix: quick command snippets (for incoming oncall)
- Check q8 warm-pool size (infra-cli): infra-cli pool list --cluster dedicated-gpu-pool-3 --model redwood/opt-q8
- Increase warm-pool (infra-cli): infra-cli pool scale-warm --cluster dedicated-gpu-pool-3 --model redwood/opt-q8 --count 3 --region us-west-2
- Autoscaler window (k8s patch): kubectl -n infra patch cm autoscaler-config -p '{"data":{"scale_in_window":"15m"}}'

Unresolved questions for follow-up
- Why did kernel-fallback path rate increase specifically for q8 models during this week? (Research)
- Do we need a new telemetry dimension to correlate client request fingerprints with cold-starts? (Observability + Product)
- Should eviction alerts be backfilled for the last 90 days to help choose thresholds? (SRE)

End of notes. Ping me on slack or page if anything is unclear — I put short-run instructions in the runbook and left links to dashboards in linked_artifacts.
